title: decision-graph-cost-advisor-and-default-templates
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: Operators need a compact, explainable way to pick batching/caching defaults and quantization profiles tuned to their workload mix without manual trial-and-error. This PR introduces a Decision Graph Cost Advisor that ingests workload traces and generates opinionated default templates (batching, prefix caching, and quant profiles) plus a lightweight CLI previewer that computes estimated unit economics for a candidate template. Changes are intentionally conservative: defaults are suggested but not auto-applied; rollout helpers are included for canarying. Summary of changes: new econ decision graph engine, CLI "rwctl cost preview", templates for batch/cache/quant, telemetry hooks for economic impact simulation, unit tests and perf smoke harness. Why this differs from prior autosuggesters: instead of a monolithic heuristic, the decision graph composes independent decision nodes (latency SLO, token distribution, cold-start ratio, model quantizability) and performs forward simulation with cost and SLA scoring to produce ranked templates and an explainable reason string. Checklist: - [x] engine implementation and tests - [x] CLI previewer + YAML template format - [x] integration with telemetry replay harness - [x] docs and rollout guide - [x] perf smoke on unit-econ simulator - [x] manual review and approvals How to validate locally: 1) run `make econ-smoke` to spin lightweight simulator with sample trace in examples/cost-presets/ 2) `./bin/rwctl cost preview --template examples/cost-presets/sample-config.yaml --trace examples/traces/chat_small.json` prints estimated tokens/cost/latency percentiles and recommended changes 3) run unit tests `go test ./pkg/econ -run TestDecisionGraph` Notes on rollout: configuration is gated behind a feature flag "econ.decision_graph.enabled" and the default templates are placed under config/econ/templates/*.yaml; operators must opt-in to apply them to runtime. The PR also documents a canary sequence: sample workload -> template apply to 5% route -> monitor econ.delta metric -> promote at 95th percentile pass threshold. Risks and mitigations: risk of over-aggressive batching harming tail latency. Mitigation: every template includes a conservative latency cap and a server-side per-route emergency throttle that will revert to previous policy when observed p99 > configured cap. Related work: builds on telemetry replay infra added in ENG-3311 and quant profile scaffolding from ENG-4120.

release_notes: Introduces Decision Graph Cost Advisor and a CLI previewer (rwctl cost preview). Adds opinionated default templates for batching, caching and quantization profiles under config/econ/templates. Feature gated behind econ.decision_graph.enabled. Includes docs and a canary rollout guide.
notes_for_oncall: If econ.delta metric spikes after applying a template, revert via rwctl policy rollback <route> and open SUP-1287. Emergency throttle will auto-revert if p99 latency exceeds template cap.
manual_steps: 1) Opt-in by toggling econ.decision_graph.enabled in configmap 2) Deploy configmap and rollout to canary routes 3) Monitor econ.delta and p99 latency 4) Promote templates gradually
testing_instructions: Run `make econ-smoke`, then `./bin/rwctl cost preview --template examples/cost-presets/sample-config.yaml --trace examples/traces/chat_small.json` and verify printed costs vs baseline; also run `go test ./pkg/econ -run TestDecisionGraph`
audit_log_summary: Added decision graph feature flag and templates; reads workload traces from telemetry; emits econ.recommendation events when previewed or applied.
changelog: Feature: Decision Graph Cost Advisor (batching/caching/quantization defaults) and CLI previewer; Docs: cost-advisor and canary sequence; Ops: smoke harness and metrics hooks
estimated_impact: Expected typical unit-cost reduction 6-18% on chat-style traces in our internal sims depending on cold-start ratio; tail-latency impact guarded by conservative caps
